Parameter reference

Source: vignettes/parameters.Rmd
parameters.Rmd

fleet is not yet validated for real use; see the status note.

This article records, argument by argument, how fleet handles the user-facing parameterisation functions of the malariasimulation individual-based model (IBM), v3.0.0: whether each argument is reproduced exactly, what is lost if not, and what to do about it. The parameters argument, the list being modified, is omitted throughout. Section references (§) are to vignette("model"); vignette("using") covers what to do differently because fleet is a mean field.

Status labels

Label Meaning Action
Exact Modelled exactly, or algebraically equivalently for the mean field None. Differences from the IBM fall within its Monte Carlo noise
Approximate Modelled, but the mean field loses something; the row says what Suitable for comparing scenarios that share the approximation. Check against the IBM if the reported result is dominated by this mechanism
Inert Accepted without error but has no effect on the run, by design rather than by omission None. Do not tune it
Ignored Not modelled; the run continues, in some cases with a warning Decide whether the run is valid without it
Unsupported Errors at input, or never reaches the model Remove it from the parameter list

Where a row carries two labels, the second is a caveat on the first.

get_parameters()

Argument malariasimulation meaning fleet
overrides Named list overriding any default parameter Exact. Passed through whole; see the breakdown by group below
parasite "falciparum" or "vivax" Exact. Both. "vivax" runs the P. vivax block (§V). MDA, SMC and PMC are refused under vivax, as malariasimulation cannot run them

overrides by group

Group Parameters fleet
Initial state proportions s_proportion, d_proportion, a_proportion, u_proportion, t_proportion Unsupported. Not read. fleet seeds at the malariaEquilibrium fixed point for init_EIR (or, under a custom demography, for the EIR the IBM’s mosquito sizing supports; see set_equilibrium()), not at user-supplied proportions
Initial immunity init_ib, init_ica, init_iva, init_icm, init_ivm, init_id, and for vivax init_iaa, init_iam, init_hyp Unsupported. Not read, for the same reason (vivax seeds at the malariaEquilibriumVivax solution)
Population size human_population Exact. Scales output counts only. The model is per capita, so run time does not depend on it
human_population_timesteps Unsupported. Not read. Population is conserved; there is no dynamic population size
Baseline demography average_age Exact. Sets η=1/average_age\eta = 1/\text{average_age}, the constant death hazard and the equilibrium age structure when custom_demography = FALSE
custom_demography Exact. Switches to the set_demography() path
Biting heterogeneity a0, rho Exact. ψi=1−ρe−ai/a0\psi_i = 1 - \rho e^{-a_i/a_0}
sigma_squared Exact. Log-normal variance of ζ\zeta
n_heterogeneity_groups Exact. Number of Gauss–Hermite nodes nzn_z. Must be a whole number ≥3\geq 3: fewer nodes are not a quadrature on the log-normal at all and only move every human off it
enable_heterogeneity Exact. FALSE collapses to a single node with ζ=1\zeta = 1. Under vivax the seed is the IBM’s for this case: everyone from the heterogeneous equilibrium’s first group, among mosquitoes sized from the whole of it (§V.6)
Aquatic mosquito del, dl, dpl, me, ml, mup, gamma Exact. Used as given in the EE/LL/PLP_L equations
Adult mosquito mum, beta, total_M, blood_meal_rates, Q0, foraging_time, species, species_proportions Exact. Per species. total_M is re-derived: from init_EIR under the default demography, and as the IBM’s own value under a custom one (set_equilibrium())
init_foim Unsupported. Not read. fleet recomputes FOIM from its own seeded human infectivity, which must be consistent with its seed
Seasonality model_seasonality, g0, g, h, rainfall_floor Exact. Truncated Fourier rainfall drives Ks(t)=K0,sscaler(t)rainfall(t)/R‾K_s(t) = K_{0,s}\,\text{scaler}(t)\,\text{rainfall}(t)/\bar{R} on a daily grid
Flexible carrying capacity carrying_capacity, carrying_capacity_timesteps Exact. See set_carrying_capacity(). carrying_capacity_scalers is not a get_parameters() default and cannot be passed in overrides; only set_carrying_capacity() creates it
carrying_capacity_values Unsupported. Not read, by fleet or by malariasimulation; only the _scalers form is used
Human disease and immunity constants dd, dt, da, du Exact. Back-translated to rD,rT,rA,rUr_D, r_T, r_A, r_U, then converted to the IBM’s per-day exit probability 1−e−1/d1-e^{-1/d} so the realised dwell matches
rb, rc, rva, rid, rm, rvm Exact. Immunity decay time constants dIB,dICA,dIVA,dIDd_{I_B}, d_{I_{CA}}, d_{I_{VA}}, d_{I_D} and the maternal decay dm,dvmd_m, d_{vm}
ub, uc, uv, ud Exact. Refractory periods, applied as ueff=⌈u⌉−1u_{\text{eff}} = \lceil u\rceil - 1 (§B.5)
pcm, pvm Exact. PMP_M, PVMP_{VM} maternal transfer fractions
b0, b1, ib0, kb Exact. bb Hill function
phi0, phi1, ic0, kc Exact. ϕ\phi Hill function
theta0, theta1, iv0, kv, fv0, av, gammav Exact. θ\theta Hill function and its age modifier fvf_v
d1, id0, kd, fd0, ad, gammad Exact. qq Hill function and its age modifier fdf_d
cd, cu, ct, gamma1 Exact. Infectivity by state. ct is superseded by the drug-linked cT(t)c_T(t) whenever clinical drugs are set
de, delay_gam, dem Exact. τE\tau_E, τl\tau_l, τM\tau_M: the three delay lines, read as the IBM reads them
Vector-control shape phi_bednets, phi_indoors, k0 Exact. Per species, in the a(t)a(t)/μ(t)\mu(t) algebra
Output bands age_group_rendering_*, incidence_rendering_*, clinical_incidence_rendering_*, severe_incidence_rendering_*, prevalence_rendering_* Exact. Each drives its own output family, as in malariasimulation (§G)
ib_/id_/ica_/iva_/icm_/ivm_rendering_*, and for vivax iaa_/iam_/hypnozoites_rendering_* Exact. Mean immunity by band, <name>_mean_*, with the band’s population as n_*, as malariasimulation renders it. idm_rendering_* names no immunity the IBM has, and renders nothing in either model
Metapopulation test-and-treat rdt_intercept, rdt_coeff Unsupported. Not read. They parameterise the PCR-to-RDT conversion used by run_metapop_simulation()’s mixing, which fleet does not support (Helpers and run functions)
Engine and solver mosquito_limit, individual_mosquitoes, r_tol, a_tol, ode_max_steps, progress_bar Unsupported. Not read. fleet is always compartmental and advances one day at a time, with no ODE solver to control
Vivax only b, f, gammal, kmax, philm_*, alm50, klm, dpcr_*, apcr50, kpcr, ca, ra, ua Exact under parasite = "vivax" (§V). Approximate: for kmax, the batch counts from 4 to kmax - 1 share levels in pairs, with a Poisson distribution inside each (§V.1); for ua, IAA’s 44-day refractory window runs as four 11-day stages (§V.3). The shared names (da, dd, dt, cd, cu, ct, rc, uc, rm, pcm, phi0, phi1, ic0, kc) carry the vivax values on a vivax list
n_with_hypnozoites_rendering_*, and incidence_relapse_rendering_* set on the list Exact. n_with_hypnozoites_*, with the band’s population as n_*, and n_inc_relapse_*

Fields specific to fleet

These four fields are not malariasimulation parameters. Each may be added to the list, and each defaults to the validated choice.

Field Default Effect
bite_dedup 1 P. falciparum only; vivax counts every bite, as the IBM does. 1 reproduces the IBM’s per-timestep bite deduplication (saturating hazard, §B.2). 0 uses the linear bεb\varepsilon that malariaEquilibrium assumes, which reduces the drift of prevalence off the seed from about 0.4% to about 0.1% at EIR 20. It does not remove it, since it changes only the hazard and not the boosting or sojourn forms. Values other than 0 or 1 (TRUE/FALSE accepted) are an error
acquired_immunity_offset 0, or 0.5 for vivax δ\delta in the bb/ϕ\phi/θ\theta Hill functions. The IBM adds 0.5 to each person’s positive acquired immunity. Falciparum reads its curves at a stratum mean, where 0 is the better match against the IBM ensemble mean; the vivax curves are read at quadrature nodes that stand for people, and take the IBM’s 0.5 (and 0 with immunity_spread = FALSE, back at the mean). Must lie in [0,1][0, 1]
immunity_spread TRUE P. vivax only. Carries the second moment of immunity in each age, heterogeneity and batch cell, and averages the immunity curves over a gamma distribution with that mean and variance (§V.3); FALSE reads them at the cell mean, with no offset. Must be TRUE or FALSE
hold_init_EIR FALSE Has an effect only under set_demography(). By default fleet matches the IBM’s mosquito density rather than its nominal EIR, so the same list realises the same transmission in both models; init_EIR is then the EIR the IBM was sized at, not the one fleet realises. TRUE seeds at init_EIR directly. Must be TRUE or FALSE

set_species()

Argument malariasimulation meaning fleet
species List of species parameter lists (gamb_params, arab_params, fun_params, kol_params, steph_params, or custom) Exact. Each entry’s blood_meal_rates, foraging_time, Q0, phi_bednets, phi_indoors and mum become per-species vectors driving an independent mosquito sub-model, coupled to the others only through the shared human population
proportions Relative abundance, summing to 1 Exact. Splits total_M and hence each species’ baseline carrying capacity. A species at proportion 0 stays inert; its K0K_0 is floored at a negligible positive value so the larval term does not evaluate 0/00/0

set_equilibrium()

Argument malariasimulation meaning fleet
init_EIR Target EIR to seed from Exact. Stored as parameters$init_EIR, which is where run_simulation_ode() reads it; the function has no init_EIR argument of its own. It means the same in both models: under the default demography it is the EIR fleet realises; under set_demography() it sizes the mosquito population exactly as the IBM’s does, and fleet seeds at the EIR that density supports (set_demography())
eq_params Custom malariaEquilibrium parameter set Exact. Merged over fleet’s own back-translation, taking precedence. set_equilibrium() writes this field even when passed NULL (storing its own back-translation), so after any call to it that stored set, not R/translate_params.R, supplies every shared constant (§F)
EIR_population_input "adult" (default) or "total" Exact. Handled upstream: malariasimulation converts a total-population EIR to adult EIR before storing it, and fleet always interprets init_EIR as adult EIR (bites per adult per year)

set_equilibrium() also calls parameterise_mosquito_equilibrium(), which sizes the adult mosquito population total_M from the human equilibrium under the IBM’s default exponential age structure (equilibrium_total_M(); custom mortality never enters). fleet never reads the stored parameters$total_M. It re-derives the quantity itself, in one of two ways:

  • Default demography. total_M is chosen so that ∑sasIM,s=init_EIR/365\sum_s a_s I_{M,s} = \text{init_EIR}/365 holds exactly under the human infectivity of fleet’s own equilibrium at the treatment coverage in force at timestep 1. This is the IBM’s formula evaluated on fleet’s grid, so the two agree up to discretisation and init_EIR is the EIR the mosquitoes deliver. The humans themselves are seeded under the coverage at timestep 0, as the IBM seeds them (§F).
  • Custom demography (set_demography()). Holding init_EIR here would give the two models different mosquito populations, and so different transmission, from the same parameter list: under the custom age structure the IBM’s mosquito density supports less (or more) transmission, and the IBM drifts there. fleet therefore reproduces the IBM’s total_M exactly (ibm_total_M(): the same human_equilibrium() call on the IBM’s 0–99.9 y grid and the same equilibrium_total_M() arithmetic), root-finds the EIR at which its own equilibrium under the custom age structure has that density, and seeds there. parameters$hold_init_EIR = TRUE seeds at init_EIR instead. Either way the seed is the malariaEquilibrium solution at that EIR, so it relaxes slightly, as every seed does (§F).

Calling parameterise_total_M() or parameterise_mosquito_equilibrium() directly does no harm and has no effect.

set_demography()

Argument malariasimulation meaning fleet
agegroups Upper edges of the death-rate age groups, in days Exact. Model age groups are binned into them by midpoint using right-closed intervals, matching .bincode(age, c(0, agegroups))
timesteps When each death-rate row takes effect Exact. Knots of a constant-interpolated μi(t)\mu_i(t), so custom demography is time-varying: a demographic transition is modelled, not frozen. Each row applies from its own timestep, as the IBM reads it (§H)
deathrates [length(timesteps) × length(agegroups)] daily death rates Exact. Used directly as μi(t)\mu_i(t). The t=0t = 0 row also sets the equilibrium age structure onto which the human seed is rescaled. The open-ended top model group is looked up one day above its lower edge, so it takes the rate of the band it belongs to rather than the one below. Approximate: model ages above the top agegroups edge take the top rate, whereas the IBM removes them. A warning is given; raise default_age_lower(max_age =) or extend agegroups to match

With a custom demography the mosquito population is sized as the IBM sizes it (see set_equilibrium()): fleet takes the IBM’s total_M and seeds at the EIR that its own equilibrium under this age structure supports, which is generally not init_EIR. An older population sustains less transmission from the same mosquitoes: the comparison article’s scenario seeds at EIR 13.9 for init_EIR = 20, matching the IBM’s realised 13.8.

set_drugs()

Argument malariasimulation meaning fleet
drugs List of 4-element vectors c(efficacy, rel_c, prophylaxis_shape, prophylaxis_scale) (for example AL_params, DHA_PQP_params, SP_AQ_params) Approximate. Each element is handled as below
  drug_efficacy Probability treatment clears the infection Exact. Multiplies coverage into ftefff_t^{\text{eff}}, and multiplies chemoprevention pulse fractions
  drug_rel_c Infectivity of a treated case relative to cd Exact. cT=cd×rel_cc_T = c_d \times \text{rel_c}, coverage-share-weighted across active drugs and time-varying
  drug_prophylaxis_shape, drug_prophylaxis_scale Weibull prophylaxis survival Exact in both moments, on the protected days a dose gives, W(1),W(2),…W(1), W(2), \dots The post-treatment chain carries the protected days left once out of TT, ∑n(1−(1−rT)n−1)W(n)\sum_n (1-(1-r_T)^{n-1})W(n) (§B.4), and its length kPk_P matches the variance of the whole T+PT + P sojourn: 9 stages for SP-AQ, 10 for DHA-PQP, 1 for AL. The chemoprevention chain, with no TT stage in front, matches the dose’s own mean and variance: 10 stages for SP-AQ, 9 for DHA-PQP. No chain has more stages than its mean has days, and none more than 20. ode_tuning(n_ph =) overrides the count. Approximate: a stage chain is not a Weibull, and it protects fully while it lasts, where the IBM’s protection is partial and fades. The TT stage adds variability the IBM’s parallel clock does not have, so for AL the protection curve is reproduced in its integral, not its shape
  drug_hypnozoite_efficacy, drug_hypnozoite_prophylaxis_shape, drug_hypnozoite_prophylaxis_scale P. vivax radical cure Exact. The treated lose every batch with the hypnozoite efficacy, drawn independently of blood-stage clearance, and start liver-stage protection: a chain of levels matched to the protected days, M2/(V+M)M^2/(V+M) stages, eleven for tafenoquine (§V.5). Approximate: a chain protects fully while it lasts; there is none where the protection ends inside the blood-stage protection given with it, as primaquine’s does inside chloroquine’s

set_clinical_treatment()

Argument malariasimulation meaning fleet
drug Index into the drug table Exact. Identifies which drug’s efficacy, rel_c and prophylaxis enter the blend
timesteps When coverage changes Exact. Knots of the step-interpolated ft(t)f_t(t) and of the drug-mix series
coverages Fraction of clinical cases treated with this drug Exact. ft(t)=min⁡(1,∑drugscovd(t))f_t(t) = \min\left(1, \sum_{\text{drugs}} \text{cov}_d(t)\right). set_clinical_treatment() errors if the summed coverage exceeds 1 at any timestep, so the cap at 1 is defensive and never binds on a valid parameter set. Approximate: the drug-linked quantities eff(t)\text{eff}(t), cT(t)c_T(t), rP(t)r_P(t) are blended by each drug’s instantaneous coverage share, so a first-line switch is modelled, but a mixed first line is represented by its blend rather than as parallel sub-populations

set_antimalarial_resistance()

Argument malariasimulation meaning fleet
drug Which clinical drug carries resistance Exact. Matched to the clinical-treatment drug index, and to the MDA, SMC and PMC drug, so a resistant chemoprevention drug clears fewer infections
timesteps When resistance levels change Exact. Knots of ETF(t)\text{ETF}(t) and SPC(t)\text{SPC}(t), merged with the treatment-coverage change times
artemisinin_resistance_proportion Fraction of infections that are artemisinin-resistant Exact. Multiplies both the ETF and SPC probabilities
partner_drug_resistance_proportion Partner-drug resistance Unsupported. malariasimulation requires 0, so it cannot reach the model
slow_parasite_clearance_probability Probability a treated resistant case clears slowly Exact. SPC(t)\text{SPC}(t), the split of the treated inflow between TT and TsT_s, coverage-share-weighted across drugs
early_treatment_failure_probability Probability treatment fails early Exact. ETF(t)\text{ETF}(t) reduces ftefff_t^{\text{eff}}, diverting those cases to DD
late_clinical_failure_probability Late clinical failure Unsupported. malariasimulation requires 0
late_parasitological_failure_probability Late parasitological failure Unsupported. malariasimulation requires 0
reinfection_during_prophylaxis_probability Reinfection while prophylactic Unsupported. malariasimulation requires 0
slow_parasite_clearance_time Mean duration of slow clearance Approximate. rTslow=1−e−1/dt_slowr_T^{\text{slow}} = 1 - e^{-1/\text{dt_slow}}, a single scalar with the same whole-day conversion as the other sojourns (§B.4). With one resistant drug the blend is exact; with several it is the coverage-weighted blend evaluated at peak resistance (peak rather than final, so a rise-then-fall schedule is not collapsed to zero)

set_bednets()

Status: approximate. Net efficacy is averaged over the net-using fraction into per-species as(t)a_s(t) and μs(t)\mu_s(t), so protection is not correlated within individuals across bites. Within that, every argument is handled exactly.

Argument malariasimulation meaning fleet
timesteps Distribution dates Exact. Every past distribution contributes: at each grid time the population is the mixture over all rounds, each weighted by its most-recent-receipt probability covd∏j>d(1−covj)\text{cov}_d\prod_{j>d}(1-\text{cov}_j)
coverages Fraction receiving a net at each distribution Exact. As above; repeated distributions accumulate rather than only the latest applying
dn0 [n_timesteps × n_species] probability a net kills a mosquito Exact. Decayed by net age: dn(sn)=dn0e−sn/γnd_{n}(s_n) = d_{n0}e^{-s_n/\gamma_n}
rn [n_timesteps × n_species] initial repelling probability Exact. Decayed towards rnm: rn(sn)=(rn−rnm)e−sn/γn+rnmr_n(s_n) = (r_n - r_{nm})e^{-s_n/\gamma_n} + r_{nm}
rnm [n_timesteps × n_species] minimum (asymptotic) repelling probability Exact. As above
gamman Insecticide decay time constant per distribution Exact. The γn\gamma_n above; each distribution decays on its own clock
retention Mean net-retention time (log-uniform model) Exact. Exponential usage survival e−sn/retentione^{-s_n/\text{retention}}
logistic_half_life, logistic_k Alternative logistic retention Exact. The survival of the IBM’s logistic retention time: S(sn)=exp⁡(−kr21−r2)S(s_n) = \exp\!\left(-k\frac{r^2}{1-r^2}\right) for r=sn/l<1r = s_n/l < 1 (else 0), with l=half_life/1−k/(k−log⁡0.5)l = \text{half_life}/\sqrt{1 - k/(k-\log 0.5)}, which gives S(half_life)=0.5S(\text{half_life}) = 0.5 exactly

set_spraying()

Status: approximate. As for nets, protection is population-averaged, and exact within that. Sprayed protection never expires in the IBM, so the mixture over past rounds has no retention factor.

Argument malariasimulation meaning fleet
timesteps Spray dates Exact. Mixture over all past rounds, weighted by most-recent-spray probability
coverages Fraction of houses sprayed Exact. As above
ls_theta, ls_gamma [n_timesteps × n_species] mortality logistic parameters Exact. ls(ss)=logit−1(θ+γss)l_s(s_s) = \text{logit}^{-1}(\theta + \gamma s_s)
ks_theta, ks_gamma Feeding-success logistic parameters Exact. ks=k0logit−1(θ+γss)k_s = k_0\,\text{logit}^{-1}(\theta + \gamma s_s)
ms_theta, ms_gamma Deterrence logistic parameters Exact. ms=logit−1(θ+γss)m_s = \text{logit}^{-1}(\theta + \gamma s_s)

The repellency rsr_s and survival sss_s derived from these are the same spray outcome per individual, so fleet forms the joint mean (1−rs)ss¯\overline{(1-r_s)s_s} rather than multiplying two independent averages. The IBM recomputes these every timestep; fleet reads as(t)a_s(t) and μs(t)\mu_s(t) once a day from series that follow the within-round logistic decay.

set_carrying_capacity()

Argument malariasimulation meaning fleet
timesteps When each scaler row takes effect Exact. Step change in Ks(t)K_s(t), composed multiplicatively with seasonality. KsK_s is read at the start of each day, as the IBM reads it, so a change scheduled for timestep tt applies from day t+1t + 1, as in the IBM (§D, §H)
carrying_capacity_scalers [n_timesteps × n_species] multipliers on baseline K0K_0 Exact. Multiplies baseline K0K_0 per species. Approximate: a scaler of exactly 0 is floored at K0×10−4K_0 \times 10^{-4} to keep the larval term finite, so complete vector elimination is approached but not reproduced exactly

set_mda() and set_smc()

set_smc() takes the same arguments as set_mda() and is handled identically.

Status: approximate. A mass campaign is applied as a pulse rather than as per-individual events, and its protection is all or nothing while it lasts. As in the IBM, the clinical and LM-detectable asymptomatic cases a round treats pass through the treated state first, detectable and infectious for the Tr stay.

Argument malariasimulation meaning fleet
drug Drug administered Exact. Its drug_efficacy scales the treated fraction. Its Weibull protection sets the chains’ means and stage counts: k=M2/(V+M)k = M^2/(V+M) for the protection from the dose, and the post-treatment rule for the protection left after the Tr stay (§B.4). Its drug_rel_c scales the infectivity of the treated. Antimalarial-resistance ETF on this drug reduces the treated fraction, and SPC sends its share of the detectable to the slow-clearing treated state
timesteps Round dates Exact. The run pauses after each round’s day; the pulse takes effect the day after the scheduled timestep
coverages Fraction of the target band reached Exact. Treated fraction =coverage×efficacy×(1−ETF)×oi= \text{coverage}\times\text{efficacy}\times(1-\text{ETF})\times o_i. A zero-coverage round has no effect
min_ages, max_ages Per-round vectors (one entry per timesteps entry) giving the target band in days, inclusive at both ends Exact. Per-round bands are honoured, each mapped onto the model age grid by fractional overlap oio_i, so narrow bands are not dropped and coarse groups are not over-treated. The absorbing top group is treated as fully covered if and only if the band reaches its lower edge. Approximate: fleet treats the band as half-open, [ℓ,u)[\ell, u), one day narrower than the IBM’s; this is negligible except for very narrow (PMC-style) bands

Co-deployed chemoprevention types (SMC, MDA, PMC) share the two chemoprevention chains, moment-matched to the mixture of their drugs’ protection. Each drug is weighted by its type’s total scheduled coverage (the sum over all its rounds), so a type with more rounds carries proportionally more weight, whatever its per-round coverage.

set_pmc()

Argument malariasimulation meaning fleet
drug Drug administered Exact. As for MDA and SMC
timesteps Coverage-change schedule (not dose dates; PMC delivery is age-triggered) Exact. Read as a coverage schedule
coverages Fraction of infants receiving each dose Exact. The coverage in force at each pulse time is used
ages Ages (days) at which doses are given Approximate. The IBM gives a dose when an individual reaches each dose age. fleet approximates this as pulses every 30 days over a 30-day band starting at each dose age, with per-group overlap weighting, keeping the effective dose at about coverage × efficacy

create_pev_profile()

Argument malariasimulation meaning fleet
vmax Maximum efficacy Exact.
alpha, beta Hill shape and scale mapping antibody titre to efficacy Exact.
cs c(mu, sigma) of log\log peak antibody titre Exact, including the sigma
rho c(mu, sigma) of the logit short-lived antibody fraction Exact, including the sigma
ds, dl c(mu, sigma) of log\log short and long antibody half-lives Exact, including the sigmas

malariasimulation re-draws all four antibody parameters from their profile distributions at every timestep, for every vaccinated individual; they are not stored per person. Population efficacy is therefore exactly 𝔼[Hill(Ab)]\mathbb{E}\left[\text{Hill}(\text{Ab})\right], not Hill(Ab at the median)\text{Hill}(\text{Ab at the median}). The sigmas are large and the Hill function is nonlinear, so the two differ materially: evaluating at the median overstated R21 efficacy by up to about 4.7 percentage points. fleet integrates over the 4-D distribution with a tensor Gauss–Hermite rule (options(fleet.pev_gq =), default 7 nodes per axis), validated against a Monte Carlo of the IBM’s own sampler to under 5×10−45\times10^{-4}. Because the IBM’s draws are independent between days and between people, there is no within-person correlation for the mean field to lose, and the quadrature is exact rather than approximate. The mean-efficacy curve is cached per profile on a daily grid.

set_pev_epi()

Status: approximate. The routine schedule and the full booster sequence are modelled; seasonal boosters are approximated, with a warning.

Argument malariasimulation meaning fleet
profile Primary-series PEV profile Exact.
coverages Coverage of the routine programme over time Exact. Time-varying: each cohort is protected at the coverage in force on its own first-dose date, not at a single coverage
timesteps When each coverage takes effect Exact. Also gates eligibility: a cohort is protected only once its first dose falls inside the programme. Gating follows malariasimulation, which keys on pev_epi_coverages/pev_epi_timesteps and never reads parameters$pev
age Age (days) at the first dose Exact. Efficacy starts at age + max(pev_doses), after the final primary dose
min_wait Minimum time since the last vaccination Inert. For a routine EPI programme this guards re-vaccination and seasonal-booster timing, not the primary-plus-booster schedule fleet models, so it has no effect on the result. For mass campaigns it does matter; see set_mass_pev()
booster_spacing Days from the final primary dose to each booster Exact. The full booster sequence is modelled: the vaccinated are partitioned by the most recent booster each has reached, and each stratum carries its own decayed efficacy
booster_coverage Matrix of conditional booster coverages Exact. Each booster’s coverage is read at its own administration date (matching coverage[match_timestep(timesteps, admin_time), booster]), which reduces to the single-row lookup in the usual case
booster_profile Per-booster profiles Exact. Each booster uses its own profile, integrated over the antibody distribution as in create_pev_profile()
seasonal_boosters Times the first booster relative to the start of the calendar year: booster_spacing[1] becomes a day of the year. It makes no reference to the fitted seasonality; the user chooses the day, for example with peak_season_offset() Approximate. Treated as a fixed days-since-primary schedule. fleet warns when this is set

set_mass_pev()

Status: approximate. Repeated campaigns are the weak point: min_wait re-vaccination exclusion is not applied, and each campaign reaches people independently of the last. A campaign’s protection ages with the cohort it vaccinated, and campaigns combine as the most recent dose, as in the IBM. A single campaign is unaffected.

Argument malariasimulation meaning fleet
profile Primary-series profile Exact.
timesteps Campaign dates Exact. The IBM keeps only the most recent vaccination per person, so the population protection is a most-recent-dose mixture, ∑kckwk∏j>k(1−cjwj)ek\sum_k c_k w_k \prod_{j>k}(1 - c_j w_j)\,e_k over completed campaigns, with ww each group’s share of a campaign’s cohort. This is the structure fleet uses for bed nets. Approximate: reaching someone in one campaign does not make them more likely to be reached in the next
coverages Coverage per campaign (recycled if length 1) Exact.
min_ages, max_ages Target age bands Exact. Every band is applied at every campaign, each mapped onto the model age grid by fractional overlap as for MDA and SMC, so a band narrower than the groups it falls between still vaccinates its share rather than nobody. The vaccinated then age: at each later day the band has moved up by the time since the campaign, so protection stays with the cohort that received it and nobody born since shares it. The bands of one campaign are one campaign: their weights add into a single covered fraction per group, capped at 1. A band overlapping no group gives a warning
min_wait Minimum time since the last vaccination Ignored, and it matters here. In malariasimulation each campaign excludes anyone vaccinated within min_wait of it, so with repeated campaigns this is the main control on who is re-vaccinated. fleet treats every campaign as reaching its whole target band independently, so a min_wait longer than the campaign spacing leads to over-vaccination
booster_spacing Days from the final primary dose to each booster Exact. Full sequence, as in set_pev_epi()
booster_coverage Conditional booster coverage matrix Exact. Read at each booster’s administration date
booster_profile Per-booster profiles Exact.

set_tbv()

Argument malariasimulation meaning fleet
timesteps Vaccination dates Exact. Antibody titre decays from each round’s date. The IBM overwrites each person’s vaccination date, and rounds combine as the most recent dose, as for mass PEV. Approximate: each round reaches people independently of the last
coverages Fraction vaccinated Exact.
ages Integer ages (years) vaccinated Exact. Each year yy is the day interval [365y,365(y+1))[365y, 365(y+1)), matched to the age groups by fractional overlap, and the vaccinated then age, the year set moving up with them. Overlap has to be fractional because, between its pinned ages, the default grid puts edges wherever its group budget falls (above 15, every 0.38 years), so a whole-year target need not line up with any group edge. A set overlapping no group gives a warning

Transmission-reducing activity is mapped to state-specific transmission-blocking activity by the IBM’s own transform TBA(mx,k,TRA)\text{TBA}(m_x, k, \text{TRA}), with per-state mx∈{𝚝𝚋𝚟_𝚖𝚞,𝚝𝚋𝚟_𝚖𝚊,𝚝𝚋𝚟_𝚖𝚍,𝚝𝚋𝚟_𝚖𝚝}m_x \in \{\texttt{tbv_mu}, \texttt{tbv_ma}, \texttt{tbv_md}, \texttt{tbv_mt}\}, giving four independent per-age multipliers on UU, AA, DD and TT infectivity. The tbv_* shape constants (tbv_tau, tbv_rho, tbv_ds, tbv_dl, tbv_tra_mu, tbv_gamma1, tbv_gamma2, tbv_k) are used as given.

set_epi_outputs()

Argument malariasimulation meaning fleet
age_group Bands for population counts Exact. n_age_*, also emitted over the union of all other families’ bands, sorted, as malariasimulation does
incidence Bands for all-infection incidence Exact. n_inc_*, and p_inc_* (0, as malariasimulation 3.0.0 renders it)
clinical_incidence Bands for clinical incidence Exact. n_inc_clinical_*, p_inc_clinical_*
severe_incidence Bands for severe incidence Exact. n_inc_severe_*, p_inc_severe_*
prevalence Bands for prevalence Exact. n_detect_lm_*, p_detect_lm_* (the expected number detected, not a prevalence), n_detect_pcr_*
ica, icm, iva, ivm, id, ib Bands for mean immunity Exact. <name>_mean_*, with the band’s population as n_*
n_with_hypnozoites, hypnozoites, iaa, iam P. vivax only Exact. n_with_hypnozoites_* and <name>_mean_*, each with the band’s population as n_*

A family whose band list is empty renders nothing, as in the IBM. A bare get_parameters() leaves four of the five families empty and sets the prevalence bands to 2–10 y, so it renders the 2–10 prevalence columns and no incidence. A band [lower, upper] holds the whole-day ages lower to upper, both ends included, and its tag is formatted as the IBM formats it (n_age_182.5_1825.5, n_inc_clinical_1e.05_2e.05). Every n_*/p_* pair is the IBM’s sampled count and its expectation; a mean field’s expected count is both.

set_parameter_draw()

Argument malariasimulation meaning fleet
draw Index 1–1000 into the fitted posterior draws Exact. malariasimulation overwrites the immunity and disease constants in the parameter list in place; they then pass through fleet’s back-translation like any other parameter. iv0 is read from the live list: set_equilibrium()’s stored copy holds malariaEquilibrium’s default whatever the draw, because malariasimulation’s back-translation table has that entry the wrong way round, and the IBM’s severe disease reads the live value. Must be called before set_equilibrium(), as in the IBM

Helpers and run functions

Function malariasimulation meaning fleet
peak_season_offset(parameters) Day of peak seasonal transmission Exact. A pure helper on g0, g and h, which fleet reads; useful for timing SMC and booster schedules
get_correlation_parameters(parameters) Correlation between intervention recipients Unsupported. Individual-level, with no mean-field analogue
run_simulation(timesteps, parameters, correlations) Run the IBM Exact. run_simulation_ode(timesteps, parameters, correlations, tuning) mirrors the first three arguments; tuning carries the discretisation settings, so nothing epidemiological sits outside the parameter list. A non-NULL correlations is ignored with a warning: the model assumes independence between interventions
run_simulation_with_repetitions(...) Repeat stochastic runs Unsupported. Not applicable: fleet is deterministic, so one run is the ensemble mean
run_metapop_simulation(timesteps, parameters, ..., export_mixing, import_mixing) Coupled patches Unsupported. fleet is a single patch. There is no guard, so a metapopulation setup passed to it is not honoured
run_resumable_simulation(...) Resume from saved state Unsupported. Not implemented. fleet runs are cheap enough to re-run from the seed
